title: Metered epochal snapshots for retroactive correction and soft-fail attribution
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Background: We continue to see edge cases where late-arriving tokens or out-of-order ingestion cause small but visible billing drift for heavy customers. Current reconciliation runs are effective, but are expensive when we need to rehydrate many intermediate states and can miss short-lived sessions. Goal: Add an epochal snapshot mechanism in the metering ingestion path that emits compact, tenant-scoped token/accounting snapshots at regular checkpoints (epoch boundaries). These snapshots will allow retroactive correction jobs to compute deltas against a stable anchor point and apply fixes with bounded work and deterministic idempotency.

Why this approach: Snapshots make corrections incremental (apply delta between snapshot and final state) and reduce reliance on full replays. They also enable safe shadow run of retroactive corrections, faster backfills, and targeted fixes for late-arrival events without touching already-stable tenants.

Scope:
- Emit checkpoint snapshots every 1h and epochal full snapshots every 24h (configurable).
- Snapshot format: tenant_id, epoch_id, token_counts_by_route (compressed), checksum, last_event_timestamp, snapshot_id (UUID).
- Store snapshots in S3 with lifecycle tags and a compact index in DynamoDB for quick lookups.
- Implement a idempotent delta applier worker that computes correction deltas from snapshot->current and writes reconciled adjustments to the billing ledger via existing idempotent write path.
- Expose metrics and tracing for snapshot emit, apply success/fail, and correction lag.

Out of scope: full reprocessing of raw events for historical windows >60d. Full ledger replays remain a separate initiative.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Snapshot writer emits schema-compliant snapshots for >99% of incoming tenants within configured epoch windows under normal load.
2) Delta applier can compute and apply corrections for a 24h window for a tenant with 1M tokens in < 10s wall time (median).
3) Shadow run against last 30 days produces identical billing outcomes for >99.95% of tenants (allowing a tolerance for known duplicates).
4) Rollout can be reversed by toggling snapshot-index reads; no customer-facing billing changes until opt-in.

Design notes:
- Snapshot writes are append-only and must never mutate existing snapshots. Corrections reference snapshot_id and produce adjustment records with origin=epochal-corrector.
- Use chunked gzip + snappy for token_counts blobs to keep S3 object sizes reasonable.
- Dynamo index stores only pointers: tenant_id -> latest_snapshot_id and epoch_id -> list(snapshot_id) (compact).
- Delta applier runs with a read-only fallback: if snapshot index is missing, it falls back to existing reconciliation path (soft-fail).

Observability:
- New metrics: snapshot_emit_success, snapshot_emit_latency_ms_p50/p95, snapshot_apply_duration_ms, snapshot_apply_errors, correction_delta_size_histogram, correction_skipped_tenants.
- Tracing tags: snapshot_id, tenant_id, epoch_id, snapshot_manifest_version.
- Dashboards: snapshot health, correction backlog, correction success rate.

Dynamo index + S3 layout + lifecycle policy (Eng: Marco)
Delta applier worker + integration with ledger write path (Eng: Liam)
Shadow run harness and verification scripts (Eng: QA + Data)
Rollout plan and feature flagging (Eng + PM)
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot writer emits for >=99% of tenants per epoch
Delta applier applies 24h tenant correction in <10s median
Shadow run shows <0.05% divergence vs current ledger
All snapshot and apply failures are surfaced to Sentry and metrics
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Schema + writer (2 sprints) -> emit snapshots to staging S3 and populate Dynamo index. Phase 2: Delta applier implementation and local end-to-end tests. Phase 3: Shadow-run of delta applier against 30-day window for a selected tenant cohort (~5% of production traffic). Phase 4: Multi-tenant canary + gradual increase with cost monitoring. Phase 5: Default on for reconciliation jobs and remove heavy replays after 60d of stable ops.
migration_plan: Backfill: initial backfill job will generate snapshots for the last 30 days for high-volume tenants only. Shadow-mode: enable delta applier in shadow (no ledger writes) for two weeks and compare correction deltas. Roll-forward: if shadow metrics within tolerance, enable corrections behind feature flag for a small percentage of tenants and monitor. If issues detected, toggle features off and notify on-call billing SRE.
testing_plan: Unit tests for serializer/validator, property tests for idempotency, integration tests with local S3 and Dynamo emulator, staging load test at 2x expected peak, and a shadow run reconciliation verification that computes diffs and checks sums. Add randomized late-event generator to validate delta correctness.
monitoring_and_alerts: Create alerts: snapshot_emit_failure_rate >1% for 10m, snapshot_apply_error_rate >0.5% for 5m, correction_backlog >10k snapshots pending. Pager escalation to billing-oncall on P0 breaches. Weekly runbook review during rollout.
risks: Snapshot storage costs higher than estimated under high tenant cardinality
Index hot keys for very large tenants leading to Dynamo throttling
Edge cases where snapshot compression loses precision (ensure checksums)
mitigations: Tiered retention: high-volume tenants have shorter snapshot retention and aggregated daily snapshots
Use batching and provisioned capacity / adaptive retry for Dynamo writes
Add checksum validation and reject snapshot emit if checksum mismatch, alerting to oncall
